Game Version Archive

Sami's game list, rebuilt as a version map.

Every spine entry is searchable now. Researched rows show the primary full-run route, secondary exclusive-content cleanup, and the platform releases that were chosen or skipped.

Open archive Method
Signature rule

Flag the conflict.

When the prettiest version cuts levels, music, modes, or story, the guide says so and gives the mop-up path.

On-stream play log

When I actually played each game.

Every day's start and stop time, the time spent that day, the running total, plus my own review and score. Built from the stream's own session logs after each broadcast.

1

Primary means fidelity plus complete package.

Resolution, frame rate, widescreen, load times, remasters, and mods matter, but not if they hide missing content.

2

Secondary means exclusive content only.

No full replay for a tiny port difference. Play the missing mission, mode, ending, boss, character, or music check and move on.

3

Unsourced claims stay untrusted.

If a port claim is not sourced, it is marked needs-review instead of being dressed up as truth.

Tamagotchi

64 de entries from Sami's spine and sourced supplemental seeds, built for per-platform route research.

Tamagotchi · 1997 64 de Hakken!! Tamagotchi Minna de Tamagotchi World

Primary full run

Original Japanese Nintendo 64 release via high-accuracy N64 emulation

Nintendo 64

There is a December 19, 1997 Nintendo 64 release and no other platform release. Because there is no PC/remaster path, the archive route is the original Japanese N64 version captured through a high-accuracy emulator for the cleanest image and stable capture.

Definitive edition

Original Japanese Nintendo 64 release

Tamagotchi · 1996 Tamagotchi

Primary full run

Generation 1 / Generation 2 original or official Original Tamagotchi rerelease

Original Tamagotchi handheld electronic game

The original Tamagotchi is a handheld virtual pet/electronic game, first released in Japan in 1996 and worldwide in 1997. Bandai's current Original Tamagotchi page says the rerelease uses the same programming as 1997, making current official hardware the practical route while vintage hardware remains the historical reference.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

Vintage hardware is historically exact; current Original Tamagotchi hardware is easier to source and uses the same 1997 programming. Choose based on whether the archive session values exact shell/history or practical play.

Definitive edition

Original Tamagotchi Generation 1 / Generation 2 handheld

Assassin's Creed · 2009 Assassin's Creed II

Primary full run

Windows version with Battle of Forli and Bonfire of the Vanities installed

Windows PC

Windows has the highest practical resolution/settings/capture ceiling for Assassin's Creed II. The game released across the original PS3/Xbox 360, Windows, OS X, Ezio Collection console, and Switch release families, plus the Battle of Forli and Bonfire of the Vanities DLC chapters. Use PC for the main run and verify the DLC/complete-content install before recording.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

The Ezio Collection is the console remaster route, while PC has the strongest capture/settings path. For Sami's archive, PC wins if the DLC chapters are installed; otherwise verify completeness before recording.

Definitive edition

Windows version with story DLC installed

Baseball · 1983 Baseball

Primary full run

Arcade Archives: Vs. Baseball

Nintendo Switch

The release family spans NES/Famicom, VS. System arcade, Game Boy, e-Reader, Virtual Console, and Nintendo Classics, with the VS. System arcade version having enhanced graphics and speech. Hamster's official Arcade Archives release is titled VS. Baseball on Switch, making it the cleanest official high-fidelity route; the NES/Famicom release remains the historical baseline but does not add exclusive content requiring a secondary run.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

Arcade Archives: Vs. Baseball is the fidelity pick because the arcade version has enhanced presentation, while NES/Famicom is the historical home baseline. No required exclusive story/career content is sourced for the NES or Game Boy routes.

Definitive edition

Arcade Archives: Vs. Baseball on Nintendo Switch

Primary full run

PlayStation 3 / Xbox 360

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

Original PC has display advantages, while original consoles had the full late DLC path; the separate Remastered entry resolves this conflict for modern play.

Mario · 2014 Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker

Sami sheet

Chosen platform Switch

Primary full run

Nintendo Switch release with Special Episode DLC and free updates

Nintendo Switch

The Switch release is the strongest main archive route because it adds Super Mario Odyssey-based courses, supports two-player local play, has the Switch-only Special Episode DLC, and there is now a free Switch 2 update with improved image quality, HDR support, and GameShare support. It is the most complete modern package, but not a total replacement for the Wii U original because the Wii U finale is framed around Super Mario 3D World while the later 3DS/Switch versions point toward Super Mario Odyssey.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

Switch with DLC is the modern completeness/fidelity winner, especially with the Switch 2 compatibility update, but the Wii U original preserves Super Mario 3D World-linked framing that differs from the later Odyssey-framed versions. Preserve Wii U as a secondary context sidebar.

Definitive edition

Nintendo Switch release with Special Episode DLC and current free updates

Sonic the Hedgehog · 1993 Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine

Primary full run

Steam / SEGA Classics Genesis version if owned

Windows

The Genesis/Mega Drive original released alongside Game Gear and Master System versions, with later Wii, Windows, 3DS, and Nintendo Switch Online access routes. Windows/SEGA Classics is the best capture route for the Genesis version if already owned, while the 8-bit Game Gear/Master System route is secondary for Puzzle Mode.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

Windows/Genesis has the best main-run fidelity and capture route, but Game Gear/Master System/3DS carry Puzzle Mode; play the Genesis version first, then the 8-bit Puzzle Mode as secondary.

Definitive edition

Windows Steam/SEGA Classics Genesis version if owned; Nintendo Switch Online Genesis version is the current official fallback

Family Computer

Famicom Disk System golf releases from Nintendo and HAL, with Disk Fax contest prize disks treated as secondary exclusive-course content.

Family Computer · 1987 Family Computer Golf: Japan Course

Primary full run

Original blue-disk Golf: Japan Course release

Family Computer Disk System

Golf: Japan Course is a February 21, 1987 NES/Famicom Disk System release developed by HAL Laboratory and published by Nintendo, with Famicom Disk System media. There is no later platform or remaster, so the highest-fidelity main route is a clean dump of the original blue disk in accurate FDS emulation. The gold prize disks add exclusive harder courses, but they replace the course content rather than serving as the normal main version.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

There is no platform fidelity split, but the normal retail blue disk is not content-complete because the Professional Course and Champions' Course prize disks contain exclusive harder course layouts. Primary stays on the retail disk; secondary covers the prize courses.

Definitive edition

Original Family Computer Disk System blue disk, plus gold-disk prize courses as secondary content

Family Computer · 1987 Family Computer Golf: U.S. Course

Primary full run

Original blue-disk Golf: U.S. Course release

Family Computer Disk System

Golf: US Course, also known as Family Computer Golf: U.S. Course, is a June 14, 1987 NES/Famicom Disk System release by HAL Laboratory and Nintendo, and is the companion to Japan Course with Disk Fax compatibility. No later platform or remaster exists, so accurate FDS emulation of the retail blue disk is the primary route; the gold Golf: Special Course prize disk is secondary because it adds a harder special course rather than replacing the normal U.S. Course.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

There is no higher-fidelity platform alternative, but content completeness requires the Golf: Special Course prize disk after the retail U.S. Course because it contains a harder special course not in the primary.

Definitive edition

Original Family Computer Disk System blue disk, plus Golf: Special Course as secondary content

Primary full run

The original game shipped first in The Orange Box and later reached Mac, Linux, Android, and Switch. Fidelity vs completeness conflict

Windows Portal with RTX is the fidelity pick for the main campaign, while the Switch Companion Collection and Xbox 360 Still Alive route are tracked for the Still Alive bonus chambers. Play the Windows RTX route first, then only the bonus chambers on a secondary platform if needed.

The Japanese Shinobi Gaisen has a unique opening, while the Western release is the practical English route with the expanded mission set; use Shinobi Gaisen only as a supplement.

THQ's MotoGP '07 released for Xbox 360, Windows, and mobile phone, but the PC version has specific issues such as a corrupt Yamaha M1 model and crowd rendering problems on post-2010 graphics drivers. Xbox 360 is the cleaner primary route; Windows and mobile have no content advantage.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

Windows would usually offer PC configurability, but sourced PC-specific issues make Xbox 360 the recommended primary.

Dungeons & Dragons video games centered on Neverwinter: the 1991 AOL graphical MMORPG, BioWare/Obsidian's Neverwinter Nights CRPG line, and Cryptic's later Neverwinter MMO. These are related by setting/brand rather than one continuous story chain.

Neverwinter · 1991 Neverwinter Nights

Primary full run

Original AOL Neverwinter Nights

MS-DOS / AOL historical service

The 1991 graphical online RPG only shipped for MS-DOS/AOL and the official online world closed in 1997, so the best route is historical preservation rather than a normal modern playthrough.

Fidelity vs completeness conflict

The only official route is historically unavailable because the AOL servers closed; there is no normal complete modern play route.

Original AOL service; no modern definitive edition
